name: LMDB
tagline: Tiny memory-mapped B+tree with ACID transactions and lock-free readers; reached 1.0 in 2026.
description: LMDB, written by Howard Chu for OpenLDAP, is a copy-on-write B+tree stored in a single memory-mapped file. Readers never block and never take locks, there is no write-ahead log or recovery step because the file is always consistent, and the whole library is a few thousand lines of C. That makes it exceptional for read-heavy embedded workloads and it is used by OpenLDAP, Monero, Postfix and many language bindings. The constraints are a single writer at a time and a file that must fit within the address space. After years on 0.9.x, LMDB 1.0 was released in 2026 with an on-disk format change, so plan a dump and reload when upgrading.

scale.notes: Single file bounded by the configured map size and virtual address space; multi-TB files work on 64-bit systems.

strengths: Lock-free, zero-copy reads directly from the memory map
Crash-proof copy-on-write design with no recovery or WAL
Full ACID transactions with MVCC snapshots
Tiny C codebase with bindings for nearly every language
Safe multi-process access to one environment
weaknesses: Only one write transaction at a time
Map size must be set up front and the file never shrinks automatically
Long-lived read transactions prevent page reuse and grow the file
1.0 changes the on-disk format; 0.9 data must be exported and reloaded
useCases: ML dataset storage with fast random reads
notIdealFor: Datasets far larger than addressable memory
